title: Microscaling Vision Transformers on FPGAs
problem: Vision Transformer models contain complex arithmetic operations (Softmax, LayerNorm) sensitive to quantization that cannot be mapped to efficient low-precision hardware. Existing methods only accelerate matrix multiplication on hardware while offloading complex operations to CPU, causing communication overhead and suboptimal performance.
motivation: Accelerating all ViT operations on FPGAs with low precision enables efficient deployment of Vision Transformers for computer vision tasks at the edge without CPU bottlenecks.
method: The authors propose an FPGA accelerator using the Microscaling Integer (MXInt) arithmetic format to quantize all ViT operations. They develop MXInt-specific approximation methods that map complex arithmetic operations (Softmax, LayerNorm) into custom hardware circuits, eliminating CPU involvement and reducing communication overhead.
key_novelty: First ViT accelerator to map all operations including complex arithmetic functions onto FPGAs using MXInt format instead of offloading to CPU.
contributions: Quantization of ViT models using MXInt format achieving high area efficiency and accuracy
MXInt-specific approximation methods for efficient hardware implementation of Softmax and LayerNorm
End-to-end FPGA accelerator achieving 93× speedup vs Float16 and 1.9× vs related work within 1% accuracy loss
Design-space exploration of tradeoffs between accuracy, hardware performance, and utilization
limitations: Limitations not explicitly discussed in abstract; evaluation scope and generalization to other ViT variants unclear.
primary_theme: Low-precision ViT FPGA acceleration via MXInt arithmetic
